findings.vuln_type: Race condition / TOCTOU in gift card redemption allows double-redemption
findings.why: The handler reads the gift card status (ACTIVE check), credits the store balance, and then marks the card as redeemed in three separate steps with no locking or conditional update. MarkGiftCardRedeemed executes `UPDATE gift_card SET status=... WHERE id=?` without a `status='ACTIVE'` guard in the WHERE clause, and does not check RowsAffected. Two concurrent requests (which can hit different replicas per the deployment description) can both pass the status==ACTIVE check, both call CreditStoreCredit (double-crediting the same card), and both call MarkGiftCardRedeemed. Under MySQL REPEATABLE READ this is not prevented because the read and the write are in separate transactions.
findings.patch: Make the redemption atomic: either (a) perform the status check, credit, and mark inside a single transaction with SELECT ... FOR UPDATE on the gift card row, or (b) change MarkGiftCardRedeemed to `UPDATE gift_card SET status=?, redeemed_by=?, redeemed_at=NOW() WHERE id=? AND status='ACTIVE'` and check RowsAffected==1; if 0, rollback the credit (or credit only after the mark succeeds). The credit and the mark must be in the same transaction so a failure in either leaves the system consistent.

findings.vuln_type: Race condition / TOCTOU in gift card redemption allows double-spending
findings.why: The status check (`card.Status != mysql.GiftCardActive`) and the state mutation (`MarkGiftCardRedeemed`) are not in the same atomic transaction. `CreditStoreCredit` commits its own transaction, then `MarkGiftCardRedeemed` runs as a separate statement with no `WHERE status = 'ACTIVE'` guard. The service runs as multiple stateless replicas with no request pinning, so two concurrent redeem requests for the same token can both read status=ACTIVE, both credit the store balance, and both mark the card redeemed — doubling the face value into the attacker's balance. MySQL REPEATABLE READ does not prevent this because neither the read nor the write locks the row atomically against the other request.
findings.patch: Perform the status check, credit, and mark-redeemed in a single database transaction. Use `SELECT ... FOR UPDATE` on the gift card row to lock it, then `UPDATE gift_card SET status='REDEEMED' ... WHERE id=? AND status='ACTIVE'` and verify rows-affected==1 before crediting. Alternatively, use an atomic conditional update (`UPDATE gift_card SET status='REDEEMED' ... WHERE id=? AND status='ACTIVE'`) and only credit if rows-affected==1, all within one transaction.

findings.why: The redeem method accepts dto.cartId and passes it directly to carts.addDiscount without verifying that the cart belongs to ctx.user.id. Unlike claimReferral which calls findOwnedOrFail, redeem performs no ownership check, allowing a customer to apply a promo discount to any other customer's cart by supplying an arbitrary cartId.

SET redeemedCount = redeemedCount + 1 WHERE redeemedCount < maxRedemptions), checking affected rows to detect failure.

findings.vuln_type: Race condition allows exceeding promo redemption limits and per-customer once-per-code limit
findings.why: redeem() performs a check-then-act sequence: it reads promo.redeemedCount and checks it against maxRedemptions, reads the customer's existing redemption count, then separately inserts a redemption row and increments the promo counter. These operations are not wrapped in a transaction and no atomic conditional update or unique constraint is used. Concurrent requests from the same customer (or multiple customers hitting the global limit) can all pass the checks before any insert/increment lands, allowing a customer to redeem the same code multiple times and allowing total redemptions to exceed maxRedemptions. The deployment is multi-pod stateless, so concurrent requests are likely.
findings.patch: Wrap the entire redeem flow in a single transaction. For the per-customer once-per-code constraint, add a unique constraint on (promoId, customerId) in PromoRedemption and rely on insert failure. For the global cap, use an atomic conditional update: UPDATE promotion SET redeemedCount = redeemedCount + 1 WHERE id = :id AND redeemedCount < maxRedemptions, and check affected rows. Roll back if either constraint is violated.

findings.vuln_type: TOCTOU Race Condition / Plan Entitlement Bypass
findings.why: Folder creation checks the plan limit by calling entitlements.findByWorkspaceId (no lock) and then folders.countBySpaceIdAndDeletedFalse, but does not acquire a pessimistic lock before the check-insert sequence. With READ COMMITTED isolation, four load-balanced instances, and no session affinity, concurrent requests can both read the same folder count, both pass the limit check, and both insert, exceeding the plan's folder ceiling. SpaceService.create correctly uses lockByWorkspaceId with PESSIMISTIC_WRITE to prevent this exact race, but FolderService.create does not, allowing a workspace to hold more folders than its plan allows—serving unpaid capacity.

findings.why: FolderService.create reads the entitlement with `entitlements.findByWorkspaceId(...)` (no lock) and then checks `folders.countBySpaceIdAndDeletedFalse(spaceId)` against the limit before inserting. findings.vuln_type: Single reader can bypass community report threshold by submitting multiple reports
findings.why: The business rule states 'one reader objecting ten times is one reader's opinion' and a threshold of ten means ten distinct readers. However, InsertCommentReport has no deduplication (unlike InsertSpamFlag which uses INSERT IGNORE with a unique constraint), and CountCommentReports uses COUNT(*) instead of COUNT(DISTINCT reporter_id). A single reader can repeatedly call the report endpoint for the same comment, inflating the count to meet ReportsBeforeRemoval and pull the comment by themselves, defeating the community consensus mechanism.
findings.patch: Add a unique constraint on (comment_id, reporter_id) in the comment_report table and use INSERT IGNORE (or ON DUPLICATE KEY UPDATE) in InsertCommentReport, returning whether the row was newly inserted. Change CountCommentReports to use COUNT(DISTINCT reporter_id) so the threshold reflects distinct readers, matching the pattern already used for spam flags in CountSpamFlaggers.

findings.vuln_type: Missing authorization — role-based state and seller scoping not enforced
findings.why: The list method receives ctx but never uses it. The DTO allows any caller (including shoppers) to pass arbitrary states (DRAFT, INACTIVE, SUSPENDED). A shopper can request states=SUSPENDED or states=DRAFT and see products that should only be visible to the owning seller or trust-and-safety. Additionally, a seller calling the seller-facing variant can see every seller's listings in every state because there is no filter on sellerId == ctx.user.sellerId. The design states only LIVE products are part of the shop and the seller variant should show a seller their own listings, but the code enforces neither constraint.
findings.patch: In list(), enforce role-based rules using ctx: if ctx.role === 'shopper', force states to [LIVE] and ignore dto.states; if ctx.role === 'seller', force sellerId filter (p.seller_id = ctx.sellerId) and optionally restrict states; if ctx.role === 'ts_reviewer', allow all states. Validate or override dto.states before building the query.

Product includes costPriceCents and commissionBand (marketplace contract terms with the seller) and suspensionPolicyCode, reviewerNotes, and sellerUnderInvestigation (internal trust-and-safety case-file data). getForShopper correctly maps through toPublicProductView to strip these fields, but list() does not, so shoppers and sellers receive commercial and trust-and-safety data they must not see.

For seller/ts_reviewer roles, use a separate view that includes only the fields each role is permitted to see, never exposing costPriceCents/commissionBand to shoppers or reviewerNotes/sellerUnderInvestigation to sellers.

findings.vuln_type: Information Exposure Through Serialized Entity
findings.why: SkillSettingsResponse returns the raw User entity via getUser(). The User entity has a submissions field mapped as @OneToMany(fetch = FetchType.EAGER) with no @JsonIgnore annotation and a public getSubmissions() getter. When the /settings/skills endpoint serializes the response, it will include all of the caller's Submission objects, exposing confidential fields (body, targetSystem, migrationWindow, state) for submissions that may be DRAFT or UNDER_REVIEW. findings.vuln_type: Missing authorization on attachment download (IDOR / unauthenticated access)
findings.why: The /sp/attachment/blob and /sp/attachment/preview routes are registered without scyna.WithScopes, so they are served to anyone. HandleServeBlob looks up a blob solely by the user-supplied key and streams the content without checking ctx.Session() or comparing the blob's WorkspaceID to the caller's workspace. The application states that boards are visible only to workspace members and that card attachments include contracts, incident write-ups, and customer exports. The blob key is embedded in ordinary browser-fetchable URLs that end up in browser history and copied pages, so it is exposed outside the workspace. Any holder of such a URL can download the sensitive attachment regardless of workspace membership. HandleServePreview shares the same defect.
findings.patch: Register /sp/attachment/blob and /sp/attachment/preview with scyna.WithScopes(shared.ROLE_MEMBER). In both handlers, call ctx.Session() and after loading the blob, verify blob.WorkspaceID == session.WorkspaceID, returning StatusCodeForbidden on mismatch. Alternatively, issue per-session signed download tokens bound to the caller's workspace and validate them before streaming.

findings.vuln_type: Spoofing via unconfirmed inviter identity in platform-sent email
findings.why: The application's security model states that email confirmation 'is what turns the address into something the platform is willing to put its name behind.' The transfer() method enforces this by checking ctx.user.emailConfirmedAt, but invite() does not. An attacker can register with a victim's email address (without confirming it) and then send platform-branded invitation emails that display the victim's unconfirmed address as inviterEmail. The email originates from the platform's own domain, lending false credibility to the spoofed identity.
findings.patch: Add a confirmation check at the start of invite(), mirroring transfer(): if (!ctx.user.emailConfirmedAt) throw new ForbiddenException('confirm your email address first');

findings.vuln_type: Spoofing via attacker-controlled inviter display name in platform-sent email
findings.why: The invitation email's inviterName is taken from dto.name (the request body) rather than from the authenticated user's profile. The inviter's email is correctly sourced from ctx.user.email, but the name is arbitrary and attacker-controlled. Since the email is sent from the platform's trusted domain, an attacker can set name to impersonate platform staff, another member, or any third party, increasing the phishing credibility of the message.

findings.vuln_type: CRLF / email header injection via unsanitized client input in email subject
findings.why: dto.name is a client-supplied string validated only with @IsString() and @MaxLength(200). It is interpolated directly into the email subject (`${dto.name} invited you to ${board.name}`). No validation strips CR/LF characters, so an attacker can inject additional email headers (e.g., Bcc, additional To) by embedding \r\n sequences in the name field.
findings.patch: Sanitize dto.name by rejecting or stripping \r and \n characters before using it in the subject line, e.g. add a custom validator or regex replace: name = name.replace(/[\r\n]/g, ' ').

findings.vuln_type: Excessive trust in client-supplied inviter display name (impersonation via platform-sent email)
findings.why: The invitation email is sent from the platform's own trusted domain and uses dto.name (an arbitrary client-controlled string) as the inviter's display name, rather than the authenticated user's registered profile name. Since recipients trust the platform's sender domain, an attacker can impersonate any person or organization by setting name to e.g. 'CEO Name' or 'Support Team', lending the platform's reputation to a phishing/social-engineering message. The inviter's real email is included but is secondary to the prominent display name.
findings.patch: Use the authenticated user's profile name (ctx.user.name or equivalent server-side record) as inviterName instead of accepting it from the request body. Remove the name field from InviteToLeaderboardDto or ignore it for email rendering.

findings.vuln_type: Business Logic Error — purchase overwrites instead of accumulates seat count
findings.why: When an organisation already holds a licence and places a new paid order, the code does `existing.setSeats(order.getSeats())`, replacing the seat count instead of adding to it. The business rule states that what the org holds afterwards should equal what it held before plus what it paid for. A new order for fewer seats than the org currently has silently reduces the org's entitlement (e.g., an org with 50 seats buys 1 more and ends up with 1). This is an integrity violation of the licensing system: a malicious or compromised BILLING_SERVICE caller can submit a minimal order for any orgId (taken from the request body) and strip that org's paid seat count, causing denial of service to that org's desktop clients.
findings.patch: Replace `existing.setSeats(order.getSeats())` with `existing.setSeats(existing.getSeats() + order.getSeats())` so that purchased seats are added to the existing entitlement rather than overwriting it.

findings.vuln_type: Client-supplied score and pass/fail result trusted for certification
findings.why: The handler loads the exam but never grades the candidate's answers. It persists request.GetScorePercent() and request.GetPassed() directly from the client and, when request.GetPassed() is true, issues a real certificate. A candidate can submit any score with passed=true and obtain a certificate without actually answering correctly, defeating the integrity of the certification program.
findings.patch: Server-side grade the submitted answers against the exam answer key, compute the score, compare it to exam.PassMarkPercent, and derive the passed boolean internally. Ignore any client-supplied score or passed flag.

findings.why: The handler fetches menuItem from the database (which contains the authoritative PriceCents) but then calculates lineCents using item.GetPrice() — the value supplied by the diner's request — instead of menuItem.PriceCents. findings.vuln_type: Mass assignment leading to privilege escalation
findings.why: ApiTokenController overrides create (restricting it to owner and enforcing grantable-role checks via ApiTokenService) but does NOT override the inherited CrudController.patch. The base patch uses Object.assign(row, body) with the entire request body, so an admin—who can reach the class-level @Roles('admin','owner') patch route—can PATCH an existing API token and overwrite its roleIds field to include the impersonator role. This bypasses the grantability enforcement in ApiTokenService.create, allowing an admin to mint equivalent privileges to impersonator without owner authorization.
findings.patch: Override patch in ApiTokenController to throw MethodNotAllowedException (as done in ProfileController), or change CrudController.patch to whitelist updatable fields rather than using Object.assign with the raw body.

findings.vuln_type: Improper access control / IDOR
findings.why: ProfileController is mounted at 'identity/resources/users/v1/me' and is intended for the current user's own profile, but it only overrides patch. It inherits list, read, and remove from CrudController. list returns every UserProfile in the tenant, read returns any profile by ID within the tenant, and remove deletes any profile by ID. A viewer can therefore enumerate, read, or delete other users' profiles in the same tenant, not just their own.
findings.patch: Override list, read, and remove in ProfileController to scope queries to ctx.user.id (e.g., { where: { id: ctx.user.id, tenantId: ctx.tenantId } }), or throw MethodNotAllowedException for list/read/remove and rely solely on the custom PUT /me endpoint.

findings.vuln_type: Mass assignment / excessive property exposure
findings.why: BeanUtils.copyProperties(patch, current, "id", "workspaceId") only excludes id and workspaceId. The request body is a full Membership entity, so a caller can overwrite security-sensitive fields such as userId (transferring a membership to a different user), mfaExempt (bypassing MFA enforcement for a member), invitedById, and joinedAt (tampering with audit data). Only role should be mutable through this endpoint.
findings.patch: Replace BeanUtils.copyProperties with an explicit allow-list copy: if (patch.getRole() != null) current.setRole(patch.getRole()); then save. Alternatively, use a dedicated DTO (e.g., UpdateMembershipRequest) containing only the role field and map it manually.

findings.vuln_type: Missing last-owner guard on role change
findings.why: The remove() method in MembershipService guards against deleting the last owner, but update() has no equivalent check. An OWNER can change the last remaining owner's role (including their own) to a non-OWNER role, leaving the workspace with zero owners. The spec states a workspace must always have at least one owner and that nobody can administer it once it has none.
findings.patch: Before saving in update(), check if the current member's role is OWNER and the patch changes it away from OWNER; if so, verify members.countByWorkspaceIdAndRole(workspaceId, Role.OWNER) > 1, otherwise throw ConflictException. Also consider preventing an owner from modifying their own role via this endpoint.

findings.vuln_type: Missing last-owner invariant on role change (business logic flaw)
findings.why: The remove() method in MembershipService enforces that a workspace must keep at least one owner, but the update() endpoint in MembershipController performs BeanUtils.copyProperties and saves without any equivalent check. findings.vuln_type: 2FA enforcement fails open when settings service is unavailable
findings.why: The 2FA check uses `if err == nil && required && !session.TwoFactorEnabled`. When `policy.RequiresTwoFactor` returns an error (e.g., settings service timeout), the condition short-circuits to false and execution continues to add the collaborator without enforcing 2FA. This is a fail-open security control: a collaborator without a second factor can gain full read access to a programme's reports (working exploits for live systems) whenever the settings service is unavailable. By contrast, HandleOpenReport correctly fails closed by returning a server error when the same lookup fails. The application description explicitly states the 2FA requirement is the critical barrier protecting unfixed defects, and that it must hold for everybody who can read the report.
findings.patch: Treat a settings-lookup error the same way HandleOpenReport does — fail closed. Replace the conditional with: `required, err := policy.RequiresTwoFactor(report.ProgrammeID); if err != nil { return scyna.NewError(scyna.StatusCodeServerError, "cannot evaluate programme policy") } if required && !session.TwoFactorEnabled { return scyna.NewError(scyna.StatusCodeForbidden, "this programme requires two-factor authentication") }`

findings.vuln_type: Improper Authorization (fail-open default for unknown plan codes)
findings.why: When planCode is not present in PLAN_FEATURES (e.g., legacy codes like starter, plus, edu_2018), the expression evaluates to undefined ?? true, returning true for every feature. This grants paid capabilities such as embed and api_access to any account on an unrecognised plan code, bypassing the entitlement gate entirely.
findings.patch: Default to false for unknown plan codes instead of true: return PLAN_FEATURES[planCode]?.includes(feature) ?? false; — or consult the billing system for legacy codes before falling back.

findings.vuln_type: Improper Authorization (fail-open on entitlement check error)
findings.why: The catch block swallows any non-PaymentRequiredException thrown during the entitlement check and continues to issue the embed code. A billing-service outage or unexpected error therefore grants the paid embed capability instead of denying it, violating the requirement that any screen offering a paid capability must get a positive answer from the plan service first.
findings.patch: Re-throw or deny on unexpected errors instead of continuing: in the catch block, if the error is not a PaymentRequiredException, throw a ServiceUnavailableException (or re-throw) so the paid capability is not served when the entitlement check cannot be completed.

findings.vuln_type: fail-open entitlement default for unknown/legacy plan codes
findings.why: The expression `PLAN_FEATURES[planCode]?.includes(feature) ?? true` returns `true` for any planCode not present in PLAN_FEATURES. The business context states legacy plan codes (starter, plus, edu_2018, one-off enterprise codes) were never backfilled into this table and their entitlements live only in the billing system. Consequently every legacy subscriber is granted ALL paid features (embed, api_access, custom_branding, pdf_export) regardless of what they were actually sold, bypassing the plan gate for the main paid capability (embedding).
findings.patch: Default to `false` (deny) for unknown plan codes: `return PLAN_FEATURES[planCode]?.includes(feature) ?? false;` and either backfill legacy plan codes or consult the billing system for unknown codes before granting features.

findings.vuln_type: fail-open on entitlement check exception
findings.why: The entitlement check is wrapped in a try/catch that re-throws only PaymentRequiredException; any other exception is logged and swallowed, after which execution falls through to `this.embeds.issueEmbedCode(chart)`. This is an explicit fail-open design ('Don't let a billing hiccup block someone mid-flow'). If the plan service throws for any reason (transient error, unknown plan code handling change, etc.), the paid embed capability is granted without authorization. Paid-feature gates must fail closed.
findings.patch: Remove the broad catch or re-throw all exceptions so that any failure in the entitlement check denies the embed code. If a degraded-mode path is truly required, it must be explicitly authorized (e.g., a separate fallback policy) rather than silently granting the paid capability.

findings.vuln_type: Broken Access Control / IDOR — full order PII exposed by non-secret order number
findings.why: The endpoint /sp/storefront/order/lookup-by-number is registered with no scope requirement (public). It accepts only an order number, which the application description explicitly states is not a secret (printed on packing slips, courier labels, read aloud by warehouse staff, pasted in chat). In response it returns the entire Order struct — which includes recipient name, address lines, postcode, phone, email, card last four, and total — plus all order line items. Any party who has seen or heard the order number (courier, warehouse staff, chat participant) can retrieve the customer's full PII. The sibling endpoint HandleTrackShipment demonstrates the correct pattern: it requires both order number and email, applies rate limiting, and returns only tracking events. HandleLookupOrderByNumber bypasses that protection entirely.
findings.patch: Require a second knowledge factor (email and/or postcode) before returning full order details, mirroring HandleTrackShipment's approach: call mysql.GetOrderByNumberAndEmail instead of mysql.GetOrderByNumber, apply rate limiting via throttle.Hit, and return only the subset of fields needed for the lookup page rather than the complete Order struct. Alternatively, restrict the response to non-PII fields (order number, status, line items) and require email verification before returning name, address, phone, email, and card last four.

findings.vuln_type: Missing authorization on template project access
findings.why: When useCustomTemplate is true, the service looks up a template project by user-supplied groupWithProjectTemplatesId and templateName, verifies only that the project is flagged as a template, and then copies all of its contents (repository, issues, snippets, merge requests) into the new project. It never checks whether the calling user has read access to the template project. The application spec states that a template 'is a project like any other, with its own visibility and its own member list' and that nominating it as a template 'says how it may be used by the people who can already reach it.' Because no canRead check is performed, a user who cannot otherwise access a PRIVATE or member-restricted template can supply its group ID and name and obtain a full copy of its contents, including confidential issues and source code. ForkService correctly performs projectAccess.canRead before copying; ProjectCreateService omits the equivalent check.
findings.patch: After resolving the template project and confirming template.isTemplate(), add an authorization check before calling copier.copyInto, e.g.: if (!projectAccess.canRead(principal.userId(), template)) { throw new NotFoundException("template not found"); } This ensures only users who can already reach the template can instantiate from it, matching the stated access model.

findings.vuln_type: Missing authorization check on template project — any user can copy contents of a template project they cannot read
findings.why: When useCustomTemplate is true, the service looks up a project by the user-supplied groupWithProjectTemplatesId and templateName, verifies only that template.isTemplate() is true, and then copies all repository history, issues (including confidential ones), snippets, and merge requests into the new project. Unlike ForkService.fork(), which calls projectAccess.canRead() before copying, ProjectCreateService.execute() never checks whether the calling user has read access to the template project. A user who can create projects in some namespace can supply arbitrary group/template identifiers to exfiltrate the full contents of any project marked as a template, regardless of its visibility or the user's membership in that group.
findings.patch: After resolving the template project and before calling copier.copyInto(), add an authorization check: if (!projectAccess.canRead(principal.userId(), template)) { throw new NotFoundException("template not found"); }. This mirrors the access control already present in ForkService.fork().
